material_definitions: The materials belong to the solid solution series Li(4-2x)MgxTi(5/3)O4.
These samples were investigated to understand the influence of magnesium substitution on the ionic conductivity of lithium titanate spinels.
The structure of the solid solution members is based on the spinel type, often compared to the parent Li4Ti5O12.
Conductivity measurements were performed using impedance spectroscopy over a temperature range from approximately 100 to 700 Celsius.
The substitution of lithium by magnesium and titanium results in changes in the concentration of charge carriers and lattice vacancies.
measurements.source_caption: Temperature dependence of the conductivity for Li3.8Mg0.1Ti1.63O4 (curve b) and Li3.4Mg0.3Ti1.53O4 (curve d) compared with Li1.33Ti1.67O4 (curve a) and Li4Ti5O12 (curve c).

material_definitions: Simple cubic perovskite La0.67-xLi3xTiO3 (x = 0.06–0.15) with disordered arrangement of the A-site ions was prepared by quenching from 1350°C into liquid N2.
Tetragonal, doubled perovskite with alternate arrangement of La-rich layers and Li-vacancy-rich layers along the c-axis was prepared by annealing the quenched pellet at 800°C for 3 days.
The lithium ion conduction in Ln0.67-xLi3xTiO3 solid solutions occurs by an ion-vacancy mechanism through the interconnecting A-sites, making a detour round Ln3+ occupied sites.
Three polymorphic forms were found in La0.67-xLi3xTiO3: high-temperature cubic form and intermediate- and low-temperature forms with tetragonal, doubled perovskite unit cells.
Site percolation is expected to be one of the determining factors for ionic conductivity in these perovskite-related structures.
